_meta.ruling: Steaming exclusion OVERTURNED. Eighth method 'gentle-heat' admitted. The enemy was never water, it was duration. R4 outranks taxonomic elegance — if a reader's redemption is steaming, the taxonomy must serve it.

reasoning.working_set: Eight methods selected. Each represents a thermodynamic or chemical category shift from the childhood failure mode (boiling). The redemption thesis is 'it was never the vegetable, it was the method' — so redemption methods must be transformations, not corrections of the same technique.
included: gentle-heat — steam or quick-blanch replacing long-boil submersion. Bright-tender result, no waterlogging. The enemy was never water, it was duration. Added per author ruling 14 Jul 2026.
char — fire replaces water; radiant/flame heat produces blackened exterior and smoky depth. Category shift: wet→dry, moderate→extreme heat.
roast — ambient convective dry heat replaces submersion; caramelisation replaces waterlogging. Category shift: wet→dry, boiled→caramelised.
blister — intense pan heat with oil replaces pot of water; concentrated exterior, retained bite. Category shift: wet→dry, passive→active.
crisp — thin-cut dehydration replaces chunk-boiling; shatter texture replaces collapse. Category shift: wet→dry, soft→brittle.
pickle — acid/salt chemistry replaces heat entirely; tang and preserved crunch. Category shift: cooked→raw, heat→chemistry.
raw-thin — precision cutting replaces any cooking; reveals what boiling hid. Category shift: cooked→raw, soft→fresh.
slow-braise — low wet heat as intention, not accident; collapse as silk, not sludge. Category shift: rushed→patient, waterlogged→concentrated.
excluded: boil — the antagonist. Not a redemption method.
microwave — a reheating technology, not a culinary method with a distinct sensory outcome.
pressure-cook — a speed variant of wet heat; does not produce a sensory outcome distinct from slow-braise for vegetables at launch scope.
confit — valid method but too niche for a vegetable-first launch taxonomy. Candidate for future 'fat' category expansion.
ferment — distinct from pickle in duration and microbial profile. Pickle covers quick-pickle and short lacto-ferment for launch; full fermentation reserved for future 'fermented' category.

methods.name: Gentle-Heat
methods.description: Steam or quick-blanch replacing long-boil submersion. Bright-tender result, no waterlogging, colour preserved. The enemy was never water, it was duration.

methods.name: Char
methods.description: Direct radiant or flame heat producing blackened, blistered exterior with smoky depth and tender interior. High heat, short duration.

methods.name: Roast
methods.description: Ambient convective dry heat producing caramelised, golden exterior and tender, concentrated interior. Medium-high heat, medium duration.

methods.name: Blister
methods.description: High pan heat with oil producing blistered, concentrated exterior while preserving interior bite and brightness. High heat, short duration.

methods.name: Crisp
methods.description: Thin-cut, high-heat dehydration producing golden, shatter-crisp texture throughout. Medium-high heat, variable duration depending on thickness.

methods.name: Pickle
methods.description: Acid, salt, or short ferment cure transforming texture and flavour without heat. Cold process, long duration. Tang, preserved crunch, brightness.

methods.name: Raw-Thin
methods.description: Mandolined or finely sliced raw preparation preserving full crunch, freshness, and cellular integrity. No heat. The vegetable as itself, revealed.

methods.name: Slow-Braise
methods.description: Low wet heat over long duration producing silky, collapse-tender texture with concentrated, sweet depth. Collapse as intention, not accident.

_singleRouteMethods.reasoning: Pickling is jar-bound by definition. Quick-pickle and lacto-ferment are both jar processes — the vessel is the method. No appliance route exists.
Raw-thin uses a mandoline or knife — these are tools, not routes. The method is 'raw preparation' and has no appliance variant. No heat, no appliance.
